flood_safety_tips.title: Move to High Ground
flood_safety_tips.text: Immediately move family, livestock, and essential belongings to higher elevations or designated shelter points as soon as rising water is observed.

flood_safety_tips.title: Never Drive or Walk in Floodwater
flood_safety_tips.text: Just 15 cm of moving floodwater can knock you down, and 30 cm can carry away a light vehicle. Turn around; do not attempt to cross flooded causeways.

flood_safety_tips.title: Beware of Fallen Electrical Lines
flood_safety_tips.text: Stay at least 10 metres away from damaged power lines, submerged transformers, and fallen cables. Report them to electrical authorities immediately.

flood_safety_tips.title: Disconnect Mains Supply
flood_safety_tips.text: Turn off the main electrical circuit breaker and LPG gas cylinder valves before leaving your home, provided you can do so safely without standing in water.

flood_safety_tips.title: Prepare an Emergency Grab Bag
flood_safety_tips.text: Keep waterproof pouches ready containing Aadhaar/identity papers, essential chronic medicines, portable torch, power bank, dry food, and clean water.

flood_safety_tips.title: Use Safe Drinking Water
flood_safety_tips.text: Floodwaters are severely contaminated with silt and sewage. Drink only boiled, chlorinated, or sealed bottled water to prevent cholera and waterborne epidemics.

flood_safety_tips.title: Monitor Verified Broadcasts
flood_safety_tips.text: Tune in to All India Radio, local district administration emergency announcements, or official NDMA disaster SMS alerts for verified evacuation updates.
